prompt: My mother is 68 and her cardiologist says she needs an aortic valve replacement. How do we choose where to have it done?
answer: Aortic valve replacement is a general term but there are actually two types. The first is aortic valve repair and the second is aortic valve replacement. These two procedures are usually done with open-heart surgery but in the case of patients who do not tolerate any major surgery, it can also be done via a heart catheterization procedure done thru the groin called an transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The repair type of surgery is not suitable for all types of damages to the heart valve. It depends on the size and shape of the damaged valve. Some valves are just impossible to repair.  The decision to repair vs replace usually depends on the size and shape of the valve.  In majority of cases, valves that can be repaired can often be repaired than replaced.  Depending on the risk factor of the patient, the different options are available.  Patients who are not a candidate for open heart will need a TAVR procedure whereas if the patient is a candidate to go thru open-heart surgery, there are multiple options depending on the size of the valve.  Once the valve is replaced, it could be biological (animal or human valve), or mechanical (stainless steel, titanium, carbon).  There are pros and cons to all three types.  Patients with mechanical valves will require blood thinners for life compared to those with biological valves.  The biological valves have a limited lifetime but they do not require blood thinners.  The risk of having blood clots after the surgery is a consideration and also some valves dilate easily after the procedures which may require a repeat surgery to exchange to a different type of valve.

It can handle large chunks of ingredients without resulting in frozen lumps. A high-speed blender also doesn’t need ice because it chops everything you put in it. In contrast, a traditional or a spinner blender, like a ninja blender, is more energy efficient at blending liquids, and super easy to clean. For just fruit and yogurt, for example, a spinner blender is perfect.

Secondly, consider your budget for the blender. High-speed blenders tend to be more expensive compared to blenders that are average blenders.

Last, figure out how large your blender should be. Smaller kitchens often have to compromise on the size of large kitchen appliances, like a blender. It is important to know which appliances fit well in small kitchens.
